skill.name: x402socks
skill.description: Use this skill when an agent needs a different source IP, rotating or geo-specific egress, or an unblocked fetch - for example "get a proxy", "route this through a proxy", "rotate my IP", "scrape without getting blocked", "anonymous proxy for an agent", "pay for a proxy with USDC", "x402 proxy", or "x402socks". It buys pay-per-use anonymous proxy egress from x402socks.com (TLS HTTP CONNECT by default, SOCKS5 opt-in), paid in USDC on Base with the x402 protocol.
skill.summary: Quote and purchase proxy access with USDC, manage credentials, and verify regional egress through TLS CONNECT.
skill.author: x402socks

security_audit.summary: Most alerts concern documented service requests, local token storage, or Markdown syntax; no evidence found of prompt injection or covert credential harvesting. Opt-in legacy transports expose reusable proxy credentials without encryption. The token writer can also disclose secrets by printing malformed responses instead of failing without response output.

remediation.issue: Legacy SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT expose reusable authentication tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Remove plaintext authentication paths or require a separately authenticated encrypted tunnel; retain TLS CONNECT as the default and reject certificate failures.

remediation.issue: Malformed or unexpected token responses are printed without redaction.
remediation.suggestion: Replace raw response output with fixed error messages, validate the response shape, and test malformed responses containing tokens for output leaks.

semantic_findings.title: Token Error Responses Can Leak Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The token writer prints raw responses when JSON parsing fails and prints non-object responses unchanged. A malformed response containing a replacement token can therefore expose it in terminal output, logs, or agent transcripts.

content.user_title: Manage x402 Proxy Access With USDC
content.value_statement: Agent workflows sometimes need a different regional egress IP without a subscription account. This skill guides approved USDC purchases, token management, and proxy verification.
actual_capabilities: Check service health and list available exits from the live node feed.
Read package entitlements and decode live payment challenges, checking every quoted amount against an optional spending cap.
Guide x402 v2 purchases with TypeScript approval policies and Python challenge-validation examples.
Store tokens with private file permissions and perform token status checks, validation, rotation, and wallet-proof recovery.
Test proxy egress using TLS CONNECT by default, with explicitly enabled legacy transport options.
Provide curl, urllib3, undici, Playwright, and Chrome proxy configuration examples.
limitations: Purchases require explicit approval, a funded USDC wallet on Base, and a compatible signing client; the shell helper does not purchase access.
Service prices, exit availability, and transport support can change; data and concurrent-session limits depend on the package.
SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT expose authentication tokens; a changed IP does not guarantee anonymity, access, or permission to automate.
Token-response error paths can print sensitive response content; the Python purchase example also requires signer integration and signing-time validation.

prompt_templates.title: Check Service Availability
prompt_templates.prompt: Check x402socks service health and list healthy, enabled exits. Identify documented TLS CONNECT options. Do not read credentials or make purchases.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Purchase Approval
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare live packages for [task] within [maximum USDC]. Retrieve a quote and list its payment terms and entitlements. Wait for explicit approval before signing.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use the existing token file to validate access and test TLS CONNECT through [exit ID]. Report the egress IP without printing credentials. Refuse plaintext fallback.

prompt_templates.prompt: Review the TypeScript purchase flow against [approved payment terms]. Check scheme, network, asset, recipient, domain, and amount at signing time. Report gaps without signing or paying.

Recover the credential through the recovery flow and confirm that replacement-token output remains private.

best_practices: Approve exact payment terms and enforce them against the challenge being signed, not only an earlier catalog quote.
Prefer verified TLS CONNECT and keep tokens in a private file, outside command arguments, source control, and transcripts.
Check live exit health and existing token status before retrying; use recovery after settled provisioning failures instead of paying again.
anti_patterns: Letting a payment wrapper sign arbitrary 402 challenges or treating a package name as spending approval.
Enabling plaintext transport on an untrusted network or disabling certificate verification to bypass connection errors.
Printing purchase or recovery responses into chat, logging credentials, or repeating a purchase after settlement.

faq.question: Does the shell helper purchase access?
faq.answer: No. It handles discovery, quotes, credentials, and egress tests. Purchasing requires a separate x402 signing client and explicit approval.

faq.question: Which payment asset and network are documented?
faq.answer: The skill documents USDC on Base. Validate the live challenge against independently approved network, asset, recipient, domain, and amount before signing.

faq.question: Where is the proxy token stored?
faq.answer: The helper defaults to the x402socks token file under the user's configuration directory with mode 0600. A configured token file takes precedence over the environment fallback.

faq.question: Are all proxy transports encrypted?
faq.answer: No. TLS CONNECT protects proxy authentication. SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT expose the reusable token and require an explicit helper opt-in.

faq.question: What happens when payment settles but provisioning fails?
faq.answer: Do not purchase again. Use the settlement transaction hash and a fresh signature from the paying wallet to request credential recovery.

faq.question: Does a proxy guarantee anonymity or target access?
faq.answer: No. It changes egress routing, but access depends on the target and service. It does not override site policies or legal obligations.
